supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: High‑octane Good Lovin’, tight Sugar Magnolia and fierce jams
ai_show_review.blurb: The show bursts with a monster 24‑minute Good Lovin’ anchored by Pigpen’s rap and Bill Kreutzmann’s driving drums. Jerry delivers powerful vocals and a wah‑wah‑laden Sugar Magnolia, while Phil’s bass dominates the high‑energy second set. Highlights include Hard To Handle, Truckin’, and the seamless China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider transition.
ai_show_review.review: April 18, 1971 finds the Dead at Lusk Field House in Cortland firing on all cylinders. From the opening of Set 1 through a marathon‑like Set 2, the band stays locked in, delivering a blistering second half that’s anchored by an astonishing 24‑minute Good Lovin’. Jerry’s vocals are as effortless as ’66, his guitar cutting through with crisp tone and a tasteful wah‑wah flourish on Sugar Magnolia. Phil’s bass is downright demonic, driving Hard To Handle and the entire set with muscular authority, even if he had a little less elbow room than usual. Pigpen shines with a primal scream on Good Lovin’ and his trademark banter before Next Time You See Me adds extra heat, while Bill Kreutzmann lays down a deep, funky groove and even takes a brief solo during the Good Lovin’ sandwich. The China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue glides smoothly, and the set closes with an uplifting Uncle John’s Band that feels like a perfect resolution to an electrifying night.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard tape with crisp, clear mix and no drop‑outs, capturing the full dynamics of the high‑energy performance.

key_highlights: Monster 24‑minute Good Lovin’ that anchors the second set.
Tight, wah‑wah‑laden Sugar Magnolia showcases Jerry’s guitar brilliance.
Pigpen’s vocal rap and banter add primal intensity to the show.
Phil’s demonic bass drives Hard To Handle and the entire set.

band_performance.Jerry: Powerful, effortless vocals and a crisp guitar tone; highlighted by wah‑wah on Sugar Magnolia and soaring leads throughout the marathon Good Lovin’.
band_performance.Phil: Dominant, demonic bass that drives Hard To Handle and underpins the high‑energy second set, though noted to have slightly less room than usual.
band_performance.Pigpen: Delivers a primal scream on Good Lovin’, rap verses that energize the crowd, and witty banter before Next Time You See Me.
band_performance.Billy: Steady, deep‑grooving drumming; provides a solid backbone and a notable drum solo during the Good Lovin’ sandwich.
